newsitem.title: USA: Bolivia races to boost natural gas production.
newsitem.headline: Bolivia races to boost natural gas production.

text.p: Bolivia is seeking to more than double natural gas production to meet demand for exports to Brazil in the coming years, state officials and industry sources said on Monday.

Brazil last year signalled its intention to take 1.1 billion cubic feet of gas in the fifth year of a 20-year supply contract, pushing Bolivia to accelerate exploration and production in the gas-prone country.
"It is not certain today whether Bolivia will have all the reserves to comply with the contract," Energy Secretary Jorge Berindoague said in a meeting with U.S. producers here.

Industry sources said Bolivian natural gas production last year was about 500 million cubic feet per day (mmcfd), including 200 mmcfd exported to Argentina. The remaining gas was either flared or reinjected to produce associated liquids.
Bolivian energy officials were in Houston on Monday courting major and independent oil and gas companies interested in bidding on exploration tracts opened up under the country's new hydrocarbon law.
The country has pegged proven reserves at 4.3 trillion cubic feet (tcf), but dedicated 7 tcf of reserves for deliveries under the Brazilian export contract, an industry source active in Bolivia said.
The Brazilian exports will flow through a 1,900 mile pipeline capitalized by a consortium led by Shell and Enron Corp slated to be in operation by 1999.

About 13 percent of the acreage targeted for exploration and production is controlled by recently capitalized Yacimiementos Petroliferos Fiscales Bolivianos (YPFB) or other producers, and the remaining 87 percent is open for bidding.
Bolivia in July will open a lease round on acreage in the central part of the country, with nominations due July 7 and awards set for September 12.
